title.narrative: UNDP Development Partner Group, DPG Support 2025-2027
UNDP Development Partner Group, DPG Support 2025-2027

description.narrative:
Projektet ska öka effektiviteten i DPG:s stöd till Etiopiens utvecklingsmål genom förbättrad koordinering och konsekvent tillämpning av principerna för effektivt utvecklingssamarbete:
-Nationellt ägarskap -Inkluderande partnerskap -Resultatfokus -Ömsesidig ansvarsskyldighet och transparens

The project will enhance the effectiveness of the development partner groups, DPG’s support for Ethiopia’s development objectives by improving coordination and applying the principles of effective development cooperation:
-National ownership -Inclusive partnerships -Results-oriented approach -Mutual accountability and transparency

The support to the DPG is expected to contribute to the following strategic goals, outcomes and outputs:
Strategic Objective:
Official Development Assistance in Ethiopia contributes, as a complement to other financing sources, to the effective implementation of the National Development Plan and the Sustainable Development Goals.
Project Outcomes:
1) Increased alignment and commitment to national development priorities by the DPG is guaranteed. 2) Transparency enhanced, and data increasingly used for effective decision making. 3) Coherent, effective and accountable policy dialogue framework.
Project Outputs:
1) Strengthened national capacity to agree through a participatory manner on and communicate national (and sub-national) development priorities through a streamlined/coherent planning framework. 2) Enhanced use and quality of development and financial data for GoE and DPG decision-making, alignment of investments to national development priorities, effective coordination across the Humanitarian-Development-Peace continuum, and diversification of financial sources for development. 3) Well managed, efficient, inclusive and strategically focused DGP structure and Secretariat.
Cross-cutting objectives
Promote gender equality and integrate a gender perspective in planning and accountability. Strengthen coordination across the humanitariandevelopmentpeace nexus. Support Ethiopias strategy for sustainable financing to diversify funding sources.

sector.narrative: Public sector policy and administrative management

description.narrative:
These are some of the results reported during the first half of the program period with some results being carried over from Phase VI. Phase VII has been operational for six months and builds on a positive previous contribution, with good prospects for strengthening donor coordination.
Output 1 Strengthened planning and monitoring systems Significant progress was made in strengthening national and sub-national planning systems, particularly through the rollout of the Digital Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation System (DPMES). This included the launch of a mobile application (ADMAS), regional readiness assessments, system customization, and training of trainers, laying the foundation for more integrated, data-driven planning and performance management across government.
Output 2 Improved data, financing frameworks, and decision-making The programme enhanced the availability and use of development and financial data through the launch of the SDG Tracker, improvements to the Aid Management Platform, and progress toward a new Aid Information Management System. At the same time, Ethiopia advanced the Integrated National Financing Framework (INFF), moving towards operational readiness with strengthened governance structures, investment planning, and partner coordination
Output 3 Strengthened coordination and policy dialogue The DPG Secretariat facilitated regular high-level coordination and policy dialogue between government and development partners, including Executive Committee and Heads of Agency meetings addressing key reform areas. Preparations for major platforms such as the High-Level Development Forum and Business Forum also progressed, contributing to improved alignment, strategic engagement, and visibility of development cooperation efforts.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
